lessons.title: When and How to Deep Condition
lessons.body: Deep conditioning is a weekly ritual for most natural hair. It restores moisture and strength after shampooing. In Africa, where hair faces sun, dust, and hard water, deep conditioning every 7â10 days is ideal. If your hair feels dry, rough, or tangles easily, it needs deep conditioning now. Use a commercial deep conditioner or a DIY mix. Start with clean, damp hair. Section hair into 4â6 parts using clips. Apply conditioner from roots to ends, but focus on ends which are older and drier. Use a wide-tooth comb to distribute evenly. For better penetration, cover with a plastic cap and sit under a hooded dryer for 15â20 minutes, or wrap a warm towel around the cap for 30 minutes. Heat opens the hair cuticle so conditioner absorbs. Rinse with cool water to seal the cuticle. If you have low porosity hair (hair that floats in water), apply conditioner to damp hair and use a steamer or warm towel. For high porosity hair (hair that sinks quickly), leave conditioner for 30 minutes without heat. Avoid applying conditioner to scalp if you have dandruff; it can worsen. After rinsing, apply a leave-in conditioner and seal with oil like shea butter or coconut oil. Deep conditioning is not a quick fix; consistency matters. Skipping it leads to breakage. In rural areas without electricity, use a warm towel method: soak a towel in hot water, wring it, and wrap around your plastic cap. Reheat towel once. Always test conditioner on a small section first to avoid allergic reactions. Deep condition at least twice a month, more if you use heat tools or live in dry climates.

lessons.title: DIY Deep Conditioners
lessons.body: You don't need expensive products to deep condition. African kitchens have powerful ingredients. Here are three tested recipes. Recipe 1: Moisture Bomb. Mix 1 ripe avocado, 2 tablespoons honey, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and 1 egg yolk. Blend until smooth. Apply to damp hair, cover with plastic cap, and leave 30 minutes. Avocado and honey are humectants, pulling moisture into hair. Recipe 2: Protein Boost. Mix 1 egg, 2 tablespoons plain yogurt, and 1 tablespoon mayonnaise. Apply to clean hair, leave 20 minutes, then rinse with cool water. Egg and yogurt provide protein; mayonnaise adds oil. Recipe 3: Aloe Vera Gel. Scoop fresh aloe gel from a leaf, blend with 1 tablespoon coconut oil and 1 teaspoon glycerin. Apply and leave 20 minutes. Aloe soothes scalp and adds shine. Always patch-test on your inner arm for 24 hours. Use fresh ingredients; discard leftovers. For dry hair, add 1 tablespoon of shea butter melted. For itchy scalp, add 5 drops of tea tree oil. Mix in a clean bowl with a spoon, not a blender if you want less mess. Apply with fingers, working from roots to ends. Detangle with a wide-tooth comb. Cover with a plastic bag or cap. For heat, wrap a warm towel over the cap. Rinse thoroughly with warm water, then cool water. Follow with a leave-in conditioner. These DIY mixes cost less than 500 naira or 50 shillings per treatment. They are chemical-free, but they spoil quickly. Make only what you need. If you have allergies to eggs or nuts, skip those recipes. For best results, use once a week. Store leftovers in the fridge for no more than 2 days. Remember: natural does not mean safe for everyone. Test first.

lessons.title: Protein Treatments: Benefits and Risks
lessons.body: Protein treatments rebuild hair that has been damaged by heat, chemicals, or rough handling. Hair is made of protein called keratin. When you dye, relax, or flat-iron, you break protein bonds. A protein treatment fills gaps and strengthens strands. Signs you need protein: hair feels mushy, stretches and breaks, or has lost its curl pattern. Use a protein treatment every 4â6 weeks. Commercial products include Aphogee Two-Step Protein Treatment or ORS Hair Mayonnaise. DIY: gelatin mask (1 packet unflavored gelatin + 1 cup warm water + 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar). Apply to clean hair, leave 15 minutes, rinse. Or use egg and yogurt as in Lesson 2. Protein treatments can be risky. Too much protein makes hair stiff, brittle, and prone to snapping. This is protein overload. Symptoms: hair feels like straw, tangles, and breaks with little stretch. If this happens, stop protein and deep condition with moisture only for 2â3 weeks. Never use protein on hair that is already brittle from lack of moisture. Always follow protein with a moisturizing deep conditioner. For low porosity hair, use light protein like yogurt. For high porosity hair, use heavier protein like gelatin. Apply protein to damp hair, not soaking wet. Leave on for the time statedâno longer. Rinse with cool water. Do not combine protein with heat unless the product says so. In Africa, many women use protein treatments before braiding or weaving to prevent breakage. But if you have fine hair, use protein sparingly. Test on a small section first. If hair feels hard after rinsing, you used too much. Next time, dilute with water or use less. Protein is not a conditioner; it is a treatment. Use it wisely.

lessons.title: Balancing Moisture and Protein
lessons.body: Healthy natural hair needs both moisture and protein. Moisture gives flexibility; protein gives strength. The balance is key. If hair breaks when dry, it needs moisture. If it breaks when wet, it needs protein. If it breaks both ways, you need both, but in the right order. Start with a protein treatment, then follow with a moisture deep conditioner. The protein fills gaps; moisture seals it in. A simple test: take a wet strand and stretch it. If it stretches a lot and doesn't bounce back, you need protein. If it snaps quickly, you need moisture. If it stretches slightly and returns, you are balanced. For most people, do a protein treatment every 4â6 weeks and a moisture deep condition weekly. After protein, always use a moisturizing conditioner. After moisture, seal with oil. Use the LOC method: Liquid (water or leave-in), Oil (coconut, olive, or shea), Cream (butter or cream). This locks in moisture. Avoid over-moisturizing: hair that feels mushy and limp needs protein. Avoid over-proteinizing: hair that feels stiff and straw-like needs moisture. In Africa, hard water can strip moisture, so you may need more moisture. Dry climates like the Sahel require more sealing oils. Humid areas like the coast need lighter products. Keep a hair journal: note what you used and how hair felt. Adjust based on results. If you relax or color your hair, you need more protein. If you are fully natural and low manipulation, you may need less. Listen to your hair. It tells you what it needs. Balance is a moving target; test and adjust.

lessons.title: Heat Therapy for Deep Conditioning
lessons.body: Heat helps deep conditioners penetrate deeper. The hair cuticle opens with warmth, allowing moisture and protein to enter. Without heat, conditioner sits on the surface. You don't need expensive tools. A hooded dryer is best: sit under it for 15â20 minutes on medium heat. If you don't have one, use a steamer. Handheld steamers are affordable and effective. Or use the warm towel method: soak a towel in hot water, wring it out, and wrap it around your plastic cap. Reheat the towel once after 10 minutes. Another method: use a thermal cap (microwaveable gel cap). Heat it in the microwave for 1â2 minutes, then wear it over your plastic cap for 20 minutes. For a DIY approach, boil water, pour into a bowl, and sit with your head over the steam (careful not to burn). Cover with a towel to trap steam. Do this for 10 minutes. Always use a plastic cap to prevent mess and trap heat. Never use direct heat like a blow dryer on high; it can fry your hair. Keep heat moderate. If you have low porosity hair, heat is essential. If you have high porosity hair, you may not need heat; just leave conditioner longer. After heat therapy, rinse with cool water to close the cuticle. Then apply leave-in and seal. Do heat therapy once a week or every two weeks. Overheating can damage hair, so limit to 20 minutes. In Africa, electricity is not always available, so the warm towel method is reliable. You can also use a black plastic bag and sit in the sun for 30 minutes. Sun heat is gentle and free. Always check the temperature on your skin before applying to hair. Safety first.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting Dry or Brittle Hair
lessons.body: Dry, brittle hair breaks and feels rough. It lacks moisture and may need protein. First, identify the cause. Is it from harsh shampoo? Hard water? Heat damage? Or medical issues like thyroid? Start by clarifying: use a sulfate-free shampoo once a month to remove buildup. Then deep condition with moisture. If hair still brittle, do a protein treatment. But if protein makes it worse, you have protein overload. Then stop protein and use only moisture for a month. For dry hair, use the LOC method daily: water, oil, cream. Seal ends with shea butter. Sleep with a satin bonnet or pillowcase to retain moisture. Avoid cotton, which sucks moisture. Wash hair in sections to reduce tangles. Use lukewarm water, not hot. Hot water strips oils. Air dry instead of blow drying. If you must use heat, use a heat protectant. Trim split ends every 8â12 weeks; split ends travel up the strand. If hair is brittle from hard water, install a shower filter or use bottled water for final rinse. In Africa, well water can be hard. Add 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar to a cup of water as a final rinse to remove minerals. For brittle hair from over-styling, take a break from braids, weaves, and tight puffs. Wear low-manipulation styles like twists or a bun. Massage scalp with oil (castor, jojoba) to stimulate blood flow. Eat protein-rich foods: eggs, beans, fish. Drink 2 liters of water daily. If hair is brittle due to medication or illness, see a doctor. If nothing works, see a trichologist. But most dryness is fixable with consistent moisture and protein balance. Track your progress weekly. Take photos. Be patient; hair grows slowly. With care, brittle hair becomes soft and strong.

quiz.q: How often should you deep condition natural hair in Africa?
options: D) Only when hair is dirty
quiz.explanation: Deep conditioning every 7â10 days restores moisture lost to sun, dust, and hard water.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of using a plastic cap during deep conditioning?
options: B) To trap heat and help conditioner penetrate
C) To prevent hair from drying
quiz.explanation: A plastic cap traps heat, which opens the hair cuticle for better absorption.

quiz.q: Which method is best for deep conditioning without electricity?
options: B) Use a warm towel over a plastic cap
C) Sit in front of a fan
quiz.explanation: A warm towel wrapped around a plastic cap provides gentle heat without electricity.

quiz.q: What should you do after rinsing out a deep conditioner?
options: B) Apply leave-in conditioner and seal with oil
D) Comb with a fine-tooth comb
quiz.explanation: Leave-in conditioner and oil seal in moisture after deep conditioning.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is a humectant in DIY deep conditioners?
quiz.explanation: Honey attracts and holds moisture from the air into the hair.

quiz.q: What is a key safety step before using a DIY deep conditioner?
options: A) Heat it in a microwave
B) Patch-test on inner arm for 24 hours
D) Use it on wet hair only
quiz.explanation: Patch-testing checks for allergic reactions before applying to the scalp.

quiz.q: Which DIY recipe is best for protein treatment?
options: D) Shea butter and coconut oil
quiz.explanation: Egg and yogurt are rich in protein, which strengthens hair.

quiz.q: How long should you leave a DIY protein mask on hair?
quiz.explanation: 15â20 minutes is enough for protein to bind without causing stiffness.

quiz.q: What is a sign that you need a protein treatment?
options: A) Hair feels mushy and stretches
B) Hair is shiny and soft
quiz.explanation: Mushy hair that stretches without bouncing back lacks protein.

quiz.q: What is protein overload?
options: B) Hair becomes stiff and brittle
quiz.explanation: Too much protein makes hair hard, straw-like, and prone to snapping.

quiz.q: How often should you use a protein treatment?
options: D) Only when hair is dirty
quiz.explanation: Every 4â6 weeks is enough to rebuild protein without causing overload.

quiz.q: What should you do if you have protein overload?
options: B) Stop protein and deep condition with moisture
quiz.explanation: Moisture-only deep conditioning restores softness and balance.

quiz.q: Which hair type should use light protein like yogurt?
quiz.explanation: Low porosity hair needs lighter protein to avoid buildup.

quiz.q: What is the best way to balance moisture and protein?
options: C) Alternate protein and moisture treatments
D) Use both at the same time
quiz.explanation: Alternating gives hair both strength and flexibility.

quiz.q: What does the LOC method stand for?
quiz.explanation: LOC stands for Liquid, Oil, Cream, used to seal in moisture.

quiz.q: Which test helps determine if hair needs protein or moisture?
options: A) Pull test on wet strand
quiz.explanation: Stretching a wet strand shows whether hair lacks protein or moisture.

quiz.q: What does hair that breaks when wet indicate?
quiz.explanation: Wet hair that snaps easily lacks protein strength.

quiz.q: How long should you use heat therapy for deep conditioning?
quiz.explanation: 15â20 minutes of moderate heat is enough to open the cuticle without damage.

quiz.q: Which tool is best for heat therapy?
quiz.explanation: A hooded dryer provides even, moderate heat for deep conditioning.

quiz.q: What is a safe DIY heat method?
options: A) Sit in sun with plastic cap
D) Use a microwave on hair
quiz.explanation: Sun heat is gentle and free, and a plastic cap traps it.

quiz.q: What should you do after heat therapy?
quiz.explanation: Cool water seals the cuticle after heat opens it.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of dry, brittle hair?
quiz.explanation: Hard water deposits minerals that strip moisture from hair.

quiz.q: Which fabric is best for sleeping to prevent dryness?
quiz.explanation: Satin retains moisture and reduces friction compared to cotton.

quiz.q: How often should you trim split ends?
quiz.explanation: Trimming every 8â12 weeks prevents split ends from traveling up the strand.

quiz.q: What is a final rinse to remove hard water minerals?
options: A) Apple cider vinegar and water
quiz.explanation: Apple cider vinegar rinses away mineral buildup and balances pH.

quiz.q: Which food helps hair strength?
quiz.explanation: Eggs are rich in protein and biotin, which support hair health.

quiz.q: What should you do if hair is brittle from over-styling?
options: B) Take a break and wear low-manipulation styles
quiz.explanation: Low-manipulation styles reduce tension and breakage.

quiz.q: How much water should you drink daily for hair health?
quiz.explanation: 2 liters of water daily supports overall hydration, including hair.

quiz.q: When should you see a doctor for brittle hair?
options: A) If it's dry after washing
B) If it's due to medication or illness
quiz.explanation: Medical causes like thyroid issues need professional diagnosis.

quiz.q: What is the best way to track hair progress?
quiz.explanation: Photos provide visual evidence of changes over time.
